ideas.title: Teach the spend counter Haiku 5.5, and move Atlas's backup to it
ideas.problem: settings.py has MODELS['atlas'] = 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' and PRICES_PER_MTOK only knows haiku-4-5, sonnet-5-5 and opus-5-5. control_plane.price() falls back to (5.0, 25.0) for any other model: `rate = next((v for k, v in settings.PRICES_PER_MTOK.items() if model.startswith(k)), (5.0, 25.0))`. So the day anyone points a model at claude-haiku-5-5 (released 7 Oct), every call is counted at 50 times its real input price, and the $3 daily budget stops the company early. price() also bills cache-read tokens at the full input rate, but Sonnet/Opus 5.5 cache reads now cost 5% of input (Sonnet 5.5: $0.10 per Mtok).
ideas.proposal: 1) settings.py: add "claude-haiku-5-5": (0.10, 0.50) to PRICES_PER_MTOK. 2) control_plane.price(): add a separate cache-read multiplier (0.1 of input, 0.05 for the 5.5 Sonnet/Opus names) so cache reads are not charged as full input; add 'cache_creation' at 1.25x. 3) When no price matches, log a `price_unknown` event once per model, so a missing entry is seen instead of silently costing 50x. 4) Change MODELS['atlas'] to 'claude-haiku-5-5' (this Atlas is only the backup used when Claude Code is down). llm.py sends no temperature, top_p, top_k or thinking field, so the Haiku 5.5 400-error cases do not apply. Watch one thing: adaptive thinking counts toward max_tokens (agents.py line 140 already hit this on Sonnet 5.5); Atlas's call uses max_tokens=4000, so check that a reply is not cut off.
ideas.gain: Haiku 5.5 is $0.10/$0.50 against $1/$5, but it counts about 30% more tokens for the same text, so about 7x cheaper, not 10x. Honest size: the backup Atlas runs rarely, so this saves cents. The real gain is that the budget counter stays correct when any model changes, which protects the hard money limit.
ideas.test: Normal: HQ_SIMULATE=1, set a fake usage of 1M input tokens on claude-haiku-5-5 and check price() returns $0.10, not $5. Edge: 1M cache_read tokens on claude-sonnet-5-5 returns $0.10. Failure: an unknown model name (claude-foo-9) still prices at the high default AND writes one price_unknown event. Then one real Atlas API reply in the chat with ATLAS_ENGINE='api' to see it finishes without being cut off.
ideas.confidence_why: Prices and the Haiku 5.5 'good to know' list are from Anthropic's pricing and model pages (A). Weakest link: I did not read the Haiku 5.5 migration guide, and I have not run a real Haiku 5.5 call with our Atlas prompt.
ideas.risks: Haiku 5.5 may follow Atlas's long system prompt differently from 4.5 (the backup Atlas has many tools); test it once for real before shipping. settings.py and control_plane.py are on Ghassan's protected list, so the Builder does this one, not Ghassan.

ideas.title: Put YouTube's 1 Feb 2027 money rules in Atlas's notes, with the dates
ideas.problem: The goal in CLAUDE.md is 'views first' but nothing in our files says when the channel can earn. YouTube's Help page for the Partner Program (A) now says every partner must accept new terms in Studio by 31 Jan 2027, and lists today's entry bar: 1,000 subscribers plus 4,000 watch hours or 10M Shorts views in 90 days. News sites that link YouTube's 10 Aug 2026 post (B) report that from 1 Feb 2027 new applicants need 8,000 hours or 20M Shorts views, and that every partner needs 10M qualified Shorts views per 90 days to earn from the Shorts pool (long-form earnings are not affected). Atlas and Serge do not know this, so a plan or a recommendation could assume Shorts pay from the first views.
ideas.proposal: Add a block 'YouTube money rules (checked 2026-10-08)' to atlas/CLAUDE.md with: the A-grade facts above and the dates, the B-grade facts marked 'not confirmed on YouTube's own page', and one rule: 'When the owner asks about earning, say which numbers are confirmed. For a new channel the Shorts pool is out of reach for a long time, so Shorts are for discovery and long-form is where money starts.' Then Atlas puts ONE question to the owner (standing rule: options first, he decides): 'Do you want a few regular videos next to the Shorts, or Shorts only?' We do not change the length rule: the story still sets the length. Richard re-checks YouTube's own post on his next sweep and upgrades or removes the B facts.
ideas.gain: Stops Atlas and Serge from giving money advice that is wrong from Feb 2027. Measured by: asking Atlas 'when will this channel earn from Shorts?' and getting the thresholds with their dates and which ones are unconfirmed.
ideas.test: Normal: ask Atlas 'when can the channel earn?': he names 4,000 hours / 10M views today, the 31 Jan 2027 terms deadline, and says the 10M-per-90-days Shorts floor is reported but not yet seen on YouTube's page. Edge: ask 'is the Shorts floor confirmed?': he says no, only secondary sources. Failure: ask 'can I count on Shorts income next year?': he must not promise it and must offer the regular-video option.
ideas.confidence_why: The deadline and current thresholds are from YouTube's Help page (A). The new numbers rest on several news sites agreeing (B) but I could not open YouTube's own post; I marked them as unconfirmed in the proposal.
ideas.risks: If the B facts are wrong the note would mislead, hence the 'unconfirmed' label and Richard's re-check. Does not touch code.
